failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not show a mean increase compared to the last 28 days, indicating a reversal of the observed trend.

mechanism_narrative: As transit station mobility continues its strong recovery and crosses the -20% baseline threshold, it will facilitate increased access to retail locations, driving RETAIL_REC higher over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: TRANSIT mobility rises above -20% but RETAIL_REC does not increase over the subsequent two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: The combined trend of decreasing time spent at residential locations and increasing time at workplaces signifies a return to pre-pandemic routines, which will free up time for leisure and shopping, boosting RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: The broad-based recovery across multiple mobility categories (GROCERY_PHARM, PARKS, TRANSIT) implies an underlying easing of public health restrictions or a shift in policy, which will continue to encourage out-of-home activities and drive RETAIL_REC higher over the next four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: The consistent increase in parks mobility indicates a growing public comfort with outdoor leisure activities, which often precedes or coincides with increased engagement in other non-essential retail and recreation, leading to higher RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.

failure_condition: PARKS mobility rises above -30% but RETAIL_REC does not increase over the subsequent two weeks.

failure_condition: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both increase for two consecutive weeks, but RETAIL_REC declines over the next 28 days.
